terms.trap: Persian puts the verb last: 'Ich müde bin'
terms.why_fields: anti_example: verb-final habit from Persian breaks verb-second

terms.trap: Persian conjugates the second verb (می‌توانم بیایم): 'Ich kann komme'
terms.scene: کمک خواستن از دوست برای جابه‌جایی
terms.why_fields: anti_example: conjugated second verb is the #1 Persian-speaker modal error

terms.job: negating a verb, adjective or statement
terms.trap: Persian negates with a prefix before the verb: 'Ich nicht komme'
terms.why_fields: anti_example: position of nicht vs Persian ن- prefix

terms.trap: Persian نباید = must not, but 'muss nicht' = don't have to
terms.why_fields: anti_example: muss nicht / darf nicht meaning flip

terms.trap: Persian progressive دارم می‌روم → 'Ich habe gehen'
using 'ich will' when ordering sounds rude
terms.why_fields: discussion: where to use it instead of will; no anti_example to avoid repeating wollen's trap

terms.job: negating a noun (no, not a, not any)
terms.trap: Persian negates the verb (پول ندارم): 'Ich habe nicht Geld'
terms.why_fields: mental_model nicht+ein makes it click; anti_example: Persian verb negation calque

terms.trap: Persian خواهم builds the future: learners read 'Ich will' as 'I will'
terms.why_fields: anti_example: wollen is not a future tense

terms.trap: None beyond darf nicht = forbidden (covered in müssen's anti_example)
terms.why_fields: discussion: Darf ich…? as the polite ask + darf nicht = forbidden

terms.job: what someone else wants you to do; advice
terms.trap: Persian باید covers both müssen and sollen
terms.scene: تلفن با همخانه پیش از خرید
terms.why_fields: anti_example: separating soll from muss for a باید speaker
